neighbours.label: the opening word of a study-design statement in a scientific abstract (Methods: this…, In this retrospective…, A questionnaire survey…)
fire: Background: Anemia is common in pregnancy. Methods: this cross-sectional study enrolled 300 women at two clinics.
Objective: to assess vitamin D levels. In this retrospective study, records of 412 patients were reviewed.
Malaria remains endemic in the region. A community-based survey was conducted among 500 households.
We describe outcomes after knee surgery. Methods: a prospective cohort of 120 adults was followed for two years.
Smoking rates among teenagers were examined. This observational study used school survey data from 2015.
Little is known about sleep in nurses. A web-based questionnaire was distributed to hospital staff in 2019.
Aims: to evaluate dental caries in children. In this descriptive study, 250 pupils were examined.
Hypertension control was assessed. Methods: this population-based study analysed data from 40 villages.
quiet: Background: Anemia is common in pregnancy and affects birth weight in many countries.
Results: vitamin D levels were lower in winter than in summer among the 412 patients.
Malaria remains endemic in the region, and children under five are most affected.
After knee surgery, most adults returned to work within three months.
Smoking rates among teenagers fell sharply after the new tax was introduced.
Nurses who work night shifts often report poor sleep and fatigue.
Dental caries was found in nearly half of the children, mostly in molars.
Conclusion: hypertension control remains poor in rural villages and needs attention.

notes: Output promotes study-type adjectives (qualitative, descriptive, observational, retrospective).
